questions.q: In the context of diffusion transformers, what is the primary architectural difference between Cross-Attention and Joint Attention?
options: Cross-Attention merges image and text tokens into a single sequence, while Joint Attention keeps them in separate streams.
Cross-Attention uses image tokens as queries and text tokens as keys/values, while Joint Attention concatenates image and text tokens so they attend to each other.
Cross-Attention is only used in UNet models, while Joint Attention is exclusively used in GANs.
Cross-Attention requires the text representation to be dynamic, while Joint Attention keeps the text representation static.
questions.answer: Cross-Attention uses image tokens as queries and text tokens as keys/values, while Joint Attention concatenates image and text tokens so they attend to each other.
questions.why: The lesson states that in Cross-Attention, 'image tokens ask questions, but they only look at the text tokens for answers' and remain separate streams. In contrast, Joint Attention involves 'image and text tokens are merged into a single, unified context. They all look at each other.'

questions.q: According to the lab results, if the query sequence length (L_q) is 4 and the key/value sequence length (L_k) is 3, what is the shape of the output tensor for Joint Attention?
options: torch.Size([1, 4, 8])
torch.Size([1, 3, 8])
torch.Size([1, 7, 8])
torch.Size([1, 12, 8])
questions.why: The lab section explicitly states: 'RESULT joint_attention_output_shape = torch.Size([1, 7, 8])' and explains that the output length is L_q + L_k (4 + 3 = 7).

questions.q: In the 'library' analogy provided in the lesson, what role do the 'librarians' play in Cross-Attention?
options: They represent the image tokens that generate the final output.
They represent the text tokens that store the information.
They represent the Queries that retrieve information from the Keys (books).
They represent the Values that are returned to the readers.
questions.answer: They represent the Queries that retrieve information from the Keys (books).
questions.why: The lesson describes the analogy: 'The readers send a librarian (the Query) to the archive. The librarian looks at the spines of the books (Keys) and pulls out the relevant pages (Values).'

questions.q: Why is it critical to slice the output in Joint Attention before passing it to the next layer?
options: To reduce the computational cost of the next layer.
To ensure that only the updated image tokens are used, preventing text tokens from corrupting the image generation.
To normalize the attention weights to sum to 1.
To convert the data type from float to integer.
questions.answer: To ensure that only the updated image tokens are used, preventing text tokens from corrupting the image generation.
questions.why: The 'Common mistakes' section states: 'In joint attention, if you forget to slice the output to extract only the image tokens, you will pass text tokens into the next layer, corrupting the image generation.'
